This creates a natural transition that signals the assistant to stop planning and start implementing the steps. I need this behavior to be consistent and automatic every time a plan is generated and presented to me.

Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

class TestAgentMemory:

        system_prompt = "This is a system prompt."
        memory = AgentMemory(system_prompt=system_prompt)
        assert memory.system_prompt.system_prompt == system_prompt
        assert memory.steps == []

    def test_return_all_code_actions(self):
        memory = AgentMemory(system_prompt="This is a system prompt.")
        memory.steps = [
            ActionStep(step_number=1, timing=Timing(start_time=0.0, end_time=1.0), code_action="print('Hello')"),

        with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError):

        model_input_messages=[ChatMessage(role=MessageRole.USER, content="Hello")],

    action_step = ActionStep(
        model_input_messages=[ChatMessage(role=MessageRole.USER, content="Hello")],

## What was changed

**`src/smolagents/memory.py`** — `PlanningStep.to_messages()` is the exact point where a presented plan is turned into conversation messages (it's how the agent's plan gets displayed and fed back into the dialogue). It now returns:

1. The plan as an **ASSISTANT** message (unchanged), immediately followed by
2. Exactly **one** **USER**-style message: `"Now go on and execute this plan."`

with a comment explaining the intent: the role change prevents the model from simply continuing to elaborate the plan message instead of acting. In **summary mode** the method still returns `[]`, so neither the plan nor the follow-up appears there — the message only ever shows when the full conversation is displayed.

## Why this spot

`PlanningStep.to_messages()` is called by `write_memory_to_messages()`, which builds the dialogue the assistant sees after each plan (initial and updated plans alike). Placing the instruction there makes the transition automatic and consistent: every time a plan is generated and shown, the assistant's next context ends with a user instruction to execute it — no manual prompting needed. This also mirrors how upstream `smolagents` implements the same pattern.

- **Unit tests**: all 10 memory tests pass; memory + agent suites together: **63 passed, 0 failures**.
- **No regressions**: I ran the full test suite before and after the change — the failure lists are byte-identical (18 pre-existing environment issues: outdated `transformers` not recognizing SmolLM2, missing `docker` module, network-dependent tests). Nothing fails because of this feature.
- **End-to-end with a fake model**:
  - Single-plan run → plan at message index 2 (ASSISTANT) → follow-up at index 3 (USER), exactly once.
  - Multi-plan run (initial + updated plan) → each plan immediately followed by exactly one follow-up, at distinct positions.
  - Summary mode → no plan content and no follow-up message anywhere.
